text:
customer-ops: Hey team — after rolling our service behind a PrivateLink endpoint/net-proxy we started seeing intermittent 502s and 401s to the Redwood API. Happens ~10% of requests, seems worse during spikes.

support-jamie: thanks for the heads up. Can you confirm this started immediately after the VPCE cutover? any recent NAT/egress policy changes?

customer-ops: yes cutover last night at 22:10 UTC. We also deployed a conditional egress policy to force traffic to corporate proxy except for allowlist to Redwood. No other infra changes.

sre-oliver: can you run a quick curl -v against the endpoint from an affected host and paste output? also dig/nslookup for the API hostname.

customer-ops: paste below.
```
$ dig api.redwood.example
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example. 60 IN A 10.0.200.45
```

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.0.200.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS unknown, Certificate status (22):
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate: CN=*.redwood-hosted.net
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< content-length: 58
{ "error": "upstream tls handshake failed: sni mismatch" }
```

network-sophie: interesting — dig returns a private IP (10.0.200.45) as expected for the VPCE. But cert CN is for *.redwood-hosted.net which implies the backend expects SNI=service.redwood-hosted.net not api.redwood.example. Are you preserving Host/SNI through your proxy/NAT?

customer-ops: our proxy rewrites Host for egress allowlist mapping (we preserve HTTP Host header but SNI is set to the original hostname by the client). We did add SNI rewrite in the proxy to map internal hostnames to external canonical hostnames for some backends — could that be it?

eng-ryan: yes that would explain intermittent 401/502s. Redwood infra will validate SNI in some routing tiers for multi-tenant handoff; if the TLS SNI doesn't match the cert (or an ACL) the connection is dropped. The fact cert CN is *.redwood-hosted.net but client SNI=api.redwood.example is a mismatch if your proxy rewrote SNI.

support-jamie: quick repro checklist: 1) from affected host run `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.200.45:443 -servername api.redwood.example` and again without `-servername` to see server cert presented; 2) capture tcpdump on host to see TLS Client Hello SNI; 3) check proxy config for any `sni` or `server_name` rewrite rules.

customer-ops: ran openssl, output below.
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.200.45:443 -servername api.redwood.example
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood Ltd, CN = Redwood CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=*.redwood-hosted.net
---
```

$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.200.45:443
CONNECTED(00000003)
Server certificate
subject=/CN=*.redwood-hosted.net

sre-oliver: both cases present same cert — which is fine. But if proxy sends SNI=redwood-hosted.net sometimes and api.redwood.example other times, the backend may route to different host/tenant or reject based on ACL. Need tcpdump to confirm client hello SNI values.

customer-ops: tcpdump shows mixed SNI: about 90% of handshakes have SNI=service.redwood-hosted.net and 10% SNI=api.redwood.example. We suspect parallel pathing: some hosts go via corporate proxy chain (which rewrites SNI) and some go directly through the VPCE to the NAT (not rewriting).

network-sophie: aha — that aligns with conditional egress policy ordering. If VPCE route + allowlist entry order isn't consistent across subnets, some packets hit the proxy path, others go straight. Check route table priority and rule ordering in your egress policy engine. Also verify source IP translation — are health checks from an NLB coming from a different IP that bypass allowlist?

customer-ops: route tables look ok but we have an older TGW propagation rule active too. Could that cause asymmetry?

eng-ryan: yes TGW + local route tables + the conditional egress engine can create sticky/different egress. Also NVAs/proxy HA pairs may distribute sessions. For immediate mitigation: 1) ensure SNI rewrite is disabled for Redwood hostnames; 2) add explicit allowlist entry for 10.0.200.45 (VPCE IP) in the proxy with passthrough (no rewrite); 3) temporarily disable TGW propagation for route table used by affected hosts.

support-jamie: also we can make Redwood accept api.redwood.example SNI for a rollout if you want — that'll reduce breakage while you fix routing. I'll coordinate with eng-runtime for a short-lived SNI alias mapping. @eng-ryan can you create a canary config?

eng-ryan: can do. I'll add an SNI alias so the routing tier accepts api.redwood.example for that VPCE range for 24h. Need client source IP ranges and example failing request IDs.

customer-ops: sending sample request IDs and our egress SNAT range: 10.0.0.0/22. Failed IDs: rwd-20250315-8a1b, rwd-20250315-8a2c.

support-jamie: thanks — I've opened an internal incident and tagged eng-runtime and eng-infra. Steps so far: reproducer curl + openssl + tcpdump, workaround plan (SNI alias + proxy passthrough), longer fix (egress policy ordering review + TGW propagation prune).

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1347 (priority P2) — eng-runtime assigned.

network-sophie: follow-up action items for customer: 1) audit proxy rules for `server_name`/SNI rewrite; 2) add explicit passthrough allowlist for VPCE CIDRs; 3) verify route table + TGW propagation ordering; 4) confirm health check source IPs and ensure they hit same egress path.

customer-ops: will run audit and schedule a TGW maintenance window. thanks all — please proceed with SNI alias and we will validate over next 24h.

eng-ryan: SNI alias applied to routing tier for 24h. monitor and ping here with results. :thumbsup:
__notes: This file contains a single continuous string of Slack-style messages for a support thread. All fields are strings or list of strings as required.
